question: Starting from rest, Raju attains a velocity of 24 m/s in a minute with his bicycle. The acceleration of the bicycle is:
solution:
The correct answer is __**0.4 m/s²**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The initial velocity (u) of Raju's bicycle is 0 m/s as he starts from rest.
 
• The final velocity (v) reached by Raju's bicycle is 24 m/s.
 
• The time (t) taken to reach this velocity is 60 seconds (1 minute).
 
• Acceleration (a) can be calculated using the formula: a=((v-u))/(t)
 
• Substituting the values: **a = (24 m/s - 0 m/s) / 60 s = 0.4 m/s²**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Acceleration**

 
 
• Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity of an object with respect to time.
 
• It is a vector quantity, which means it has both magnitude and direction.
 
• Common units of acceleration are meters per second squared (m/s²).
 
 
 
• **Velocity**
 
 
• Velocity is the speed of an object in a given direction.
 
• It is also a vector quantity.
 
• The SI unit of velocity is meters per second (m/s).
 
 
 
• **Distance and Displacement**
 
 
• Distance is the total path covered by an object, irrespective of direction.
 
• Displacement is the shortest distance from the initial to the final position of an object in a straight line.
 
• Both are measured in meters (m).
 
 
 
• **Kinematic Equations**
 
 
• Kinematic equations relate the motion of an object to time, velocity, acceleration, and displacement.
 
• They are used to solve problems involving linear motion with constant acceleration.
 
• Examples include: 
 
 
• v=u+at
 
• s=ut+(1)/(2)at²
 
• v²=u²+2as
